text:
sam: ran a big offline replay overnight with the new prefetch-demographics sampler, noticed weird tail latency bump around 95th-99th percentiles :thinking_face:

maria: curious — is that with the new bucketization or just sampler change?

sam: sampler + slight bucketization tweak. short summary: throughput ok, median latency stable, tail up ~18-22% on p99 for seq_len > 1024. added logs and traces in the replay artifacts.

josh: can you paste the replay config? especially token_budget and queue policy

sam: sure — config used:

```
batcher: 
  token_budget_target: 48
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  prefetch_sampler: demographics_v2
  bucketize_by: "seq_len:quantiles(8)"
  queue_policy: age_weighted+size_bias
  kv_prefetch_ratio: 0.12
```

sam: also ran kernel selection with fallback on heavy sequences, didn't force int8 so kernels were mixed.

anya: I bet KV cache cold startup + bucket skew causes oversized batches that trigger slower kernel path on a few requests. did you capture kv_hit_rate by bucket?

sam: not by bucket, only overall. overall kv_hit_rate was 0.68, but traces show cold stretches for some tenant cohorts.

perf-bot: perf report attached: flamegraph + callcounts (link) — notable stalls in kv_miss_handler and a few memcpy spikes around kernel_bind.

kevin: question: the sampler demographics_v2 — does it bias toward long-tail tenants? if so that would explain bucket population shift and token_budget being exceeded for some batches.

maria: if prefetch_ratio is low, KV misses cause on-the-fly syncs and block batch formation, increasing latency. raising prefetch_ratio or prewarming hot keys might help.

josh: I'd try two quick repros: (A) increase token_budget_target to 64 and prefetch_ratio to 0.25; (B) keep token_budget=48 but force deterministic bucket weights (no age bias). run replay A/B and compare p50/p95/p99 and kv_hit_by_bucket.

sam: started run A now. scheduling B next. logs show one regression case where kernel_selector picked the slower aten_cuda path instead of fused_flash for a 2k token sequence when batch had mixed seq lengths.

anya: that's the kernel-selection heuristic failing on mixed-length batches — we should add a quick check in selector: if max_seq>threshold and avg_seq_ratio>0.8 then prefer fused_flash. low-cost guard.

kevin: agreed. also add a metric: kernel_choice_by_batch_shape so we can correlate.

perf-bot: A run finished: p50 12ms (same), p95 +6%, p99 +20%. kv_hit_rate overall improved to 0.74 with prefetch_ratio 0.25 but tail still high for long sequences. attaching sampled traces.

sam: B run (deterministic weights) queued, ETA ~20m. initial thought: bucketization quantiles are moving long sequences into small buckets that starve batcher eviction heuristics, causing more heterogeneous batches.

maria: maybe increase number of buckets for >1024 tokens (split high tail) so bucketizer doesn't lump 1k-2k and 2k-4k together.

josh: i'll spin a replay with bucket_count_high_tail=4 and run the ab harness across 24h to get stable numbers.

anya: also add an AB eval harness metric for "kv_warmup_time_ms" per tenant so we can see which cohorts need targeted prewarming.

sam: ack — will modify harness config and push. tagging @kevin for rollout PR once we have small config changes validated.

deploy-bot: job scheduled: replay-ab-run-1903214567-A (sam) -> started (nodes=12, sim_days=2)

sam: thanks all. plan: (1) finish B job, (2) run bucket-tail split test, (3) land selector guard and metric, (4) re-run AB for 48h. will post updated perf summary and selection rationale. :thumbsup:
